subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.
reasoning:
I'm planning a substantial module, aiming for a rich build with 150+ parts and multiple textures depicting Baku, the Japanese chimera spirit—combining a tapir's trunk, tiger paws, ox tail, lion mane, and rhino-like eyes with elephant tusks, rendered in bold ukiyo-e style with flat colors, ink outlines, and indigo blues.

Now I'm working out the design specifics: a quadruped roughly 1.8m long with a barrel-shaped tapir body, prehensile trunk, small round ears, flame-like mane blades along the neck and back, lion-style clawed paws, and a tufted ox tail. I'm considering an indigo body with cream saddle markings reminiscent of a Malayan tapir, decorated with seigaiha wave patterns and swirling cloud motifs across the flanks and shoulders in traditional Japanese decorative style.

Writing the wave-pattern shader logic...

For overlap order, I'll pick whichever candidate circle has the lowest center so the lower rows draw on top, giving that classic fan-shaped visible arc, then derive the ring color from the distance bands. This should be cheap enough to run per texel.

For the black outlines ukiyo-e needs, true backside-hull duplication isn't easy here since I can't control material side per mesh, so I'll skip that approach and instead fake the outline effect using ink line details within the paint functions themselves.

For extruded flat shapes like mane blades, I realize I can paint the extrude's thin side walls (where the normal is roughly perpendicular to the thickness direction) as dark ink rims, giving a convincing outlined look without any hull trick. That should work nicely for flat decorative elements, eyes, claws, and toe lines, even if tube geometry won't get the same treatment.

Now I'm shifting to the rig itself, thinking through the rest pose and the joint chain needed for spine, neck, head, jaw, and trunk.

I'm sketching actual scale and skeleton coordinates: a stylized tapir-like body roughly 1.15m at the shoulder, facing +Z, resting on the ground plane, with an arched back that peaks at the rump and a root hip joint, working out approximate spine joint positions from hips through chest to the neck base.

Now I'm setting up the hips as the root joint with a spine role, chaining the spine joints outward from that same position, and starting to define the tail chain.

Adding a cow-like tail hanging from the hips with a tuft at the end, then beginning the leg definitions with the front legs' shoulder and foot positions using a three-segment limb.

Defining the paw as a flattened sphere with small toe bumps and curved claw cones attached to the wrist joint, then moving on to set up the hind leg hip-to-target geometry symmetrically on both sides.

For front legs I'll use two segments with the elbow bending back, tapering the thickness from thigh to paw. I'm considering coloring: indigo legs with cream socks evoking a tapir, maybe gold cuff bands at the wrists for ukiyo-e flair, but keeping it simple. For the body I'll loft along the spine using a hip-to-spine bone chain with a radius sweep function.

Still plotting spine points...

I'm tapering the body radii from rump to chest to neck, shifting the belly down slightly for clearance above the legs, checking the resulting proportions look right for a tapir, then moving on to the coat coloring with an indigo body and cream saddle band.

Writing the cream saddle band with a seigaiha wave pattern in pale blue, defining the palette of indigo, cream, vermilion, gold, sumi, peach, and wave blue, and starting the paint function that draws a wavy-edged saddle shape across the midsection...

Adding swirling cloud and flame-scroll decals in vermilion and gold to the shoulders and haunches, like ornamental spiral motifs, then moving into the baku's head design with a long trunk-like proboscis, tusks, ox-like ears, and rhino-style eyes.

I'm setting up the neck chain joints connecting the body to the head, then building the skull and muzzle shapes, extending the tapir-like proboscis forward with an upper lip that drapes over the lower jaw using a swept joint chain.

Now I'm mapping out the trunk's joint points, curving it forward and down from the nose base, then experimenting with having the tip curl upward slightly like an elephant's trunk, since this is meant to be a fantastical baku creature rather than a realistic tapir.

I want to add wrinkle rings along the trunk by painting darker bands based on the stripe pattern along its length, keeping the base color indigo with a cream-pink tip. Then I'm sketching the jaw as a small wedge beneath the muzzle.

For the mouth structure, I'm placing the upper jaw as a muzzle block from the cranium to the nose base, with the lower jaw hinging at a joint and angling forward and slightly up, both tapering toward the front. I'll add small conical teeth along both jaws, a flat red tongue slab, and curved boar-like tusks sprouting from the sides of the upper jaw in cream-gold.

Now I'm working out the baku's elephant-like tusks curving forward and down from the muzzle sides using small bezier sweeps, then moving to the eyes—designing fierce ukiyo-e style eyes with sumi outlines, gold irises, and red accent streaks, placed as decals on the sides-front of the skull sphere.

Adding bold flame-shaped vermilion brow ridges above the eyes, and designing round tapir-like ears with cream rims using layered extrusions (indigo outer, pink inner) positioned upright at the top of the cranium.

Still working out ear orientation vectors...

Since mirroring always flips handedness, I'll determine the front-facing sign from the ear's axis dot product with forward-Z, then place the inner detail layer offset slightly along that axis using the same x,y directions scaled down for the smaller outline. Now I'm moving on to designing the mane as flame-like blades in vermilion, gold, and indigo running along the neck and back.

I'm planning a helper function for building individual flame-shaped blades with curved S-curve outlines and root-to-tip color gradients, arranged along the neck's dorsal line and cheek areas with alternating tilts and offsets so they layer naturally like ukiyo-e lion mane curls.

Still working out blade orientation...

I'm planning a paint factory for the mane that creates a color gradient along each blade's length—indigo near the root, transitioning to vermilion, then gold at the tip—plus a cream center streak, using rim-based ink detection for wall edges.

Since true wall detection needs directional info I don't have, I'm weighing whether to create a separate paint per blade versus simplifying by skipping ink rims entirely and just relying on the gradient for visual separation to save on cost.

Actually, I'm reconsidering: per-blade paint cost is manageable for ~60 small blades, but maybe a flat color plus a slightly larger dark extrude behind for outline would be simpler, though that doubles the part count. I'm also thinking SVG texture cards could work well for mane tufts — a flame-shaped blade drawn with ink outlines and a root-to-tip color gradient, applied to cards as a single part, which could be cheaper than per-blade geometry approaches.

I decide to combine both techniques: cards with flowing ink-outlined flame shapes and hair-line details for most of the mane, ruffs, tail tuft, and eyebrows, plus a handful of hero extruded curls along the neck and back crest for emphasis. Given I can't test the code before running it, I need to be conservative and stick to well-documented API patterns to avoid crashes.

Setting up the imports and beginning the geometry builder...

I'm planning to use the glow kit sparingly — maybe for the dream orb and possibly the eyes — while keeping materials simple (flat colors, standard mesh materials) so nothing breaks. I'm also considering adding a small swirling dream-cloud effect to reinforce the "dream-eating" theme.

Defining color constants...

Still defining the saddle zone...

Still working out texture coordinates...

Now I'm thinking through the seigaiha wave pattern coloring, defining concentric rings in cream and blue at different distance thresholds to create the traditional layered fan shape.

For the coat, I'm shifting to indigo outside the saddle region with darker mottling, a darker navy underside, and adding thin vermilion and gold border lines marking the transition between saddle and indigo zones.

I'm also layering in subtle noise-based contour lines on the indigo to mimic bokashi gradation and woodblock texture, giving the night-sky effect ukiyo-e prints use.

Defining more paint variants...

Rounding out the texture list: eye, cloud-spiral scroll decals for the flank, flame mane cards in both vermilion-gold and indigo-white variants, an ox-tail tuft texture, and maybe a small forehead emblem like a gold tomoe circle instead of a full collar or sash.

I'm also considering a dream-bubble effect near the trunk tip — a tiny glowing card with a moon or crane motif, floating just in front of the trunk, maybe attached to a trunk-tip bone so it hovers with a slight swirl connecting it back.

For facial markings, I'm debating tiger-like ink stripe decals across the forehead and cheeks, but they'd be invisible against the dark indigo face. I'm leaning toward giving the head a cream-colored muzzle patch like a tapir to create contrast for the stripes to show up against.

Defining leg paint logic...

For the tail, I'm thinking a thin indigo sweep ending in a cream tuft made of leaf-shaped texture cards plus a core, maybe ringed with cards at the tip. As for horns, I'm considering skipping them since baku traditionally feature an elephant trunk and rhino-like eyes rather than ox horns.

Deciding against horns to avoid overcrowding the head, I'll add a forehead jewel or gold tomoe disk instead. Now I'm setting up the head's joint structure, positioning the neck chain and head base, and defining the head's local coordinate orientation for forward-facing features.

Placing the cranium using local coordinates with a slight forward and upward offset, scaled to roughly 0.17 by 0.16 by 0.2 in world space, keeping things simple by skipping extra region constants.

Now I'm setting up the head joint at the end of the neck chain with a downward-forward direction, explicitly parenting it to the last neck joint, then sweeping the neck chain with varying radii in the base color.

Defining the neck and spine chains...

Still working out the body curve points and radius tapering...

Now I'm placing scroll decals on the body surface, positioning them at the flank, shoulder, and hip with mirrored coordinates per side, making sure the decal orientation reads correctly when viewed from outside.

For the cloud-spiral scroll SVG, I'm sketching a transparent-background karakusa-style design with a large vermilion swirl outlined in dark ink, plus a smaller secondary spiral and gold accent dots.

Now moving to the eye design at 256px size, I'm drawing an almond-shaped ukiyo-e eye with an ink outline, white sclera, gold-orange iris, and a vermilion kumadori streak at the outer corner.

Writing SVG path data...

Adjusting the brow stroke position...

Now I'm placing the eye decals using spherical coordinates on the skull, computing the hit point by azimuth and elevation from the skull center, then mirroring placement for the opposite side while accounting for a possible null hit and the head's slight downward tilt.

For the muzzle, I'm building a tapered box from the skull center forward to get that blocky puppet look, shrinking the width and height toward the tip, and planning a color gradient for the muzzle surface.

Above that, I'm placing the trunk base at the front of the muzzle and sketching a joint chain that descends forward then curls upward near the tip, working out coordinates point by point to get a natural hanging-and-curling shape.

I'm treating the trunk as a tentacle-type chain parented to the head, with four spans between the five points, each span becoming its own joint. For the tip, I'm planning a tapering sweep radius and a wrinkle texture made of thin dark rings along the trunk's length, blending from a cream base color toward the tip.

Now I'm deciding the trunk's palette, settling on indigo gradating to cream muzzle tones, and adding a small cream finger-spike at the very tip like an elephant's trunk end, plus a dark nostril disc. I'm also sketching a dream-wisp effect: a glowing violet-white spiral sweep emanating from the nostril, tapering from a thicker to thinner radius, alongside a textured plane positioned near the trunk tip to act as a dream bubble.

Reconsidering placement though — I don't want anything floating directly in front of the face occluding it, so I'm shifting the dream element to the side rather than centered, and ultimately deciding to simplify by dropping the bubble card entirely in favor of just a glowing spiral wisp curling beside the trunk tip, as if dreams are being drawn in.

Setting the card to use frames facing up with flow pointing along +Z so the face reads correctly to a viewer in front, and attaching it to the trunk tip joint.

I need to confirm glow() accepts the array of card meshes directly, since the material gets cloned per texture/tint. Now I'm defining the jaw joint off the head, using local coordinates for positioning and aim, then building the lower jaw box with a frustum shape between two jaw-relative points.

Working through the muzzle and jaw geometry: positioning the upper muzzle box, placing the jaw hinge below it, and sizing the lower jaw box so its top edge sits just under the muzzle bottom with a slight gap to keep the mouth from looking fully closed.

Deciding against the curving whisker approach as too costly, I move on to placing the ears relative to the head joint's local coordinate frame, working out the ear base position and starting to sketch the round ear outline shape.

Adjusting the ear outline to be symmetric about the base, extending outward and upward with appropriate orientation vectors so the ear angles correctly off the skull.

For the ear, I'll layer three scaled-down extrusions on top of each other—cream for the outer rim, indigo at 0.82 scale, and pink at 0.55 scale—each offset slightly forward along the thickness axis so they stack visibly without z-fighting.

Right, Part.local handles that conversion. Now I'm planning counts and placement: fourteen neck crest blades, five spine blades, cheek ruffs on both sides, a chest ruff hanging beneath the neck, plus tail and leg tufts at elbows, hocks, and fetlocks to match the flame-fur style of a karashishi/baku figure.

I'm memoizing by thickness and length so similar blades can reuse cached results, and setting up palette variations -- a vermilion/gold set for the neck mane and an indigo-to-white set for the back crest -- with the palette id folded into the memo key. Now I'm laying out the tail chain with five points running from the rump down to the tip, using four tapering spans with decreasing radii, making sure the tail start sits inside the body sweep's rump cap. Then I'm working on cheek ruffs and a mane-like ring of blades around the back of the head, placing them with varying elevation and length so they fan outward and backward like a lion's mane, considering using a ring helper around the head bone with outward-facing directions for each blade.

I'm positioning the mane blades to fan radially around the skull like a lion's ruff, spacing 12 of them so they don't collide with the ears or crest by adjusting their forward offset and skipping the frontmost index.

Now I'm working out the brow shapes — flame-like swooshes placed above each eye socket, calculating their position by projecting onto the skull sphere using azimuth and elevation angles against the skull's center and radii.

Sketching the brow outline as a flame-like shape with a sharp tip, positioned above the eye with outward and upward offsets.

Still working out brow placement...

For the forehead emblem, I'll place a tomoe decal near the top-front of the skull, sized around 0.09, rendered as a gold disc with an ink outline and three vermilion comma-shaped tomoe rotated around the center for the classic triple-swirl look.

Now I'm adding cheek stripe decals—curved tapering ink strokes mirrored on each side below the eyes, sized around 0.12 by 0.1, and considering whether to add a chest medallion or necklace element next.

For the necklace, I'm placing a ring of jade magatama-style beads around the neck base at roughly t=0.35, matching the neck radius there (~0.2) and setting bead spheres slightly outside that radius so they sit embedded—using a ring of 16 small jade spheres at radius just over the neck's.

The necklace beads sit a bit lower on the neck so they'll overlap slightly with the mane coverage, which is fine. For the paws, I'm working out each one as a scaled pad sphere with four toe spheres and ivory claw cones, positioning them relative to the foot joint with specific offsets for toe spacing.

Writing paw and leg geometry...

Now I'm working through the hind leg placement, figuring out how the thigh bulk and hip joint positions relate to the body's rump radius so the legs attach naturally at the body surface rather than floating outside it.

For the front legs, I'm computing root and foot positions, then calling a limb function to generate bone chains with bend hints so the elbow flexes backward realistically, naming each joint in the chain and setting the parent attachment point at the chest/spine.

For gold accents, I'm adding small torus bracelets at the wrists, orienting them flat so the ring sits horizontally around the limb.

For the leg ring position, I'll use the chain's parametric point near the lower section (t≈0.88) to get the center, matching the tube radius slightly larger than the leg's own radius there so it sits just outside the surface. Then I'm thinking about adding elbow fur tufts as small blades angled back from the joint.

Now I'm planning flame-like blade clusters at the front elbow and hind hock, pointing backward with slight upward/outward tilt, and also a crest line of blades running along the dorsal spine from shoulder to rump using the body's sweep function for positioning, colored with the indigo/wave/white palette.

Setting up the surface points for blade embedding, then working out the chest ruff's hanging blades with downward-back directions, and starting to define color palettes for fire and wave themes.

Adding up legs, paws with toes and claws, cuffs, ears, tusks, teeth, eyes, stripes, scrolls, blades, necklace, and tail segments brings the total part count to roughly 190. I'm also cataloging the distinct textures needed — eye, scroll, tomoe, stripes, flame cards, dream — about seven total, plus several paint variants for base, coat, trunk, leg, and muzzle.

I'm figuring out the overlap order: picking the circle with the lowest center to draw on top means lower rows shingle over upper ones, so the visible parts form upward-opening arcs like waves, matching the seigaiha pattern rather than fish-scale shingling.

Now I'm assigning ring colors based on distance bands, using a deep blue outline for the outermost ring and progressively lighter shades toward a cream center. I'm starting to write the coat-painting function that adds wobbly, sinusoidal variation to simulate a saddle pattern's irregular edges.
